text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.

- Vice president Godfrey Miyanda on Thursday assured Zambians that elections would be held this year and dismissed as seditious, opposition statements that there would be no government after October 31 if elections were not held by then.

- The government is introduce new laws that will enable it to regulate the activities of non-governmental organisations, vice president Godfrey Miyanda told Parlaiment on Thursday. The laws would enable it check the activities of "erring" NGOs.
- Government nurses at Lusaka's University Teaching Hospital called off a strike for more pay on Thursday after union leaders said they would negotiate new pay packages for them.
- The Commonwealth Health Community said it was impressed with health reforms being undertaken by the government.
